questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The general solution of $\sin x-\cos x=\sqrt{2}$, for any integer $n$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{ll}\text{ Given, } & \sin x-\cos x=\sqrt{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \sin x-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cos x=1 \\ \Rightarrow & \sin x \cdot \sin\frac{\pi}{4}-\cos x \cdot \cos\frac{\pi}{4}=1 \\ \Rightarrow & -\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=+1 \\ \Rightarrow & \cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\cos \pi \\ \Rightarrow & x+\frac{\pi}{4}=2 n \pi+\pi \\ \therefore & x=2 n \pi+\frac{3 \pi}{4}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
If $\cos \alpha+2 \cos \beta+3 \cos \gamma=0$,
$\sin \alpha+2 \sin \beta+3 \sin \gamma=0$ and $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=\pi$, then $\sin 3 \alpha+8 \sin 3 \beta+27 \sin 3 \gamma$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $a=\cos \alpha+i \sin \alpha\quad b=\cos \beta+i \sin \beta$ and $\mathrm{c}=\cos \gamma+i \sin \gamma$
Then, $a+2 b+3 c=(\cos \alpha+2 \cos \beta+3 \cos \gamma)\quad+i(\sin \alpha+2 \sin \beta+3 \sin \gamma)=0\Rightarrow \quad a^{3}+8 b^{3}+27 c^{3}=18 a b c\left(\because\right.$ if $\left.x+y+z=0 \Rightarrow x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3}=3 x y z\right)\Rightarrow \quad \cos 3 \alpha+8 \cos 3 \beta+27 \cos 3 \gamma$ and $\quad \sin 3 \alpha+8 \sin 3 \beta+27 \sin 3 \gamma\quad=18 \sin (\alpha+\beta+\gamma)=18 \sin \pi=0$

questions.solution:
Given, $\sin 2 x=4 \cos x
\begin{aligned}$&\Rightarrow \quad 2 \sin x \cos x=4 \cos x \\
&\Rightarrow \quad 2 \cos x(\sin x-2)=0
\end{aligned} $\Rightarrow \sin x=2$, which is not possible because the value of $\sin x$ lies between $-1$ and 1.
$\therefore \quad \cos \mathrm{x}=0\Rightarrow \quad x=2 n \pi \pm \frac{\pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of solutions for the equation $\sin 2 x+\cos 4 x=2$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\sin 2 x+\cos 4 x=2
\begin{array}{ll}
\Rightarrow$& \sin 2 x+1-2 \sin ^{2} 2 x=2 \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \sin ^{2} 2 x-\sin 2 x+1=0
\end{array} Now, Discriminant, $\mathrm{D}=(-1)^{2}-4 \cdot 2 \cdot 1=-7 < 0$
Hence, it is an imaginary equation, so the real roots does not exist.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin 3 \theta=\sin \theta$, how many solutions exist such that $-2 \pi < \theta < 2 \pi$ ?
questions.solution:
We have, $\sin 3 \theta=\sin \theta
\begin{aligned}&\Rightarrow \quad \sin 3 \theta-\sin \theta=0 \\ \text{$ and $} \Rightarrow 2 \cos \left(\frac{3 \theta+\theta}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{3 \theta-\theta}{2}\right)=0 \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \cos 2 \theta \cdot \sin \theta=0 \quad \cos 2 \theta=0 \quad \text{ or } \sin \theta=0, \pi,2 \pi\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad \cos 2 \theta=\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \text{ or } \quad \theta=0, \pi=2 \pi\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \quad \theta=0, \pi,2 \pi\\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow \quad \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{7 \pi}{4} \quad \text{ or } \quad \theta=0, \pi,2 \pi\\ \text{ and } \because \quad \theta=0, \pi,2 \pi
\end{aligned}$ Thus, total number of solutions $=7$
